Recovery

Neil Han
Blockchain Scalability Book · Neil Han
Scalability is not one number.
Trace the whole path. State the assumptions. Test the claim.
Blockchain scalability is often reduced to one number: transactions per second. That
number hides the real engineering questions. Which resource becomes scarce? Who
verifies the work? What data remains available? Which trust assumption changed? What
happens when the sequencer, prover, bridge, committee, or governance process fails?
Blockchain Scalability Book follows transactions and failures end to end across Layer
1, Layer 2, payment channels, rollups, modular data availability, parallel execution,
and consensus. Neil Han explains each mechanism with explicit security assumptions,
worked calculations, operational recovery paths, and methods for evaluating benchmark
claims. Written for master's students, lecturers, protocol engineers, researchers,
architects, technical founders, and analysts, the book includes graduate-level
exercises and solution sketches, threat-model worksheets, a practitioner evaluation
handbook, and a reusable benchmark-reporting template.
• Decompose any TPS claim into resource and trust constraints
• Trace normal and failure paths across L1, L2, rollups, bridges, and data availability
• Reproduce throughput, sampling, and committee calculations with explicit units
• Audit benchmark claims with a reusable reporting template
• Compare systems by threat model and recovery, not headline numbers
Neil Han is a blockchain engineer and educator. He developed
this book from graduate teaching and production protocol work.
Free digital editions: neilydhan.github.io/Blockchain-Scalability-Book
